content.title: About
content.content: Queso Fresco is a fresh solid cheese made from whole cow’s milk. It has a mild, slightly tangy flavor, a crumbly yet firm texture, and a pale white color. It is commonly used in salads, Mexican dishes, and as a standalone snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Queso Fresco is traditionally produced in Latin America, especially Mexico and Central America.
The cheese is not aged long, retaining a high moisture content (about 55%).
Unlike many aged cheeses, Queso Fresco contains no added enzymes or spices.
It crumbles easily and is often used as a feta substitute in recipes.
Fresh production preserves a high amount of calcium and milk protein.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Queso Fresco provides about 18 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Approximately 200 mg of calcium per 100 g helps strengthen bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The cheese contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Low lactose content
items.content: During fermentation some lactose is converted, making the cheese often tolerable for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Zinc and selenium in the cheese contribute to normal immune function.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey protein may experience reactions when consuming this cheese.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The cheese can be moderately salty; those monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Short shelf life
items.content: High moisture makes the cheese prone to rapid spoilage and bacterial growth if not stored properly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cube Queso Fresco into salads, crumble it over tacos, use it in burrito fillings, or enjoy it as a light snack. It can also be lightly pan‑fried for a golden crust.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cheese in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C. Consume within 5‑7 days after opening. Discard if it develops an ammonia smell or visible mold.
